Now I have a clear picture of what farmers like me in Quzhou County actually do. Let me give you my plan.

I am a 50-year-old farmer in Quzhou County with 30 years of experience. My family has 5 people, and some of them work off-farm, so I cannot spend all day in the fields. I have 7.8 mu of land and a well for irrigation. I grow wheat, maize, and cotton. My main cropping system is wheat-maize double cropping, which feeds my family, and I keep a smaller plot of cotton for cash income.

At the start of this growing season, my winter wheat is already in the field — I sowed it last October after rotary tillage. Right now it is greening up, and I need to apply the first topdressing of nitrogen and irrigate once to help it recover from winter dormancy. I will irrigate two more times before harvest: once at the jointing stage and once during grain filling. For wheat, I use improved seed — Luyuan 502 or Jimai 22, varieties I have trusted for years. I apply about 35 kg of nitrogen per mu, mostly as urea and compound fertilizer, plus some phosphate and potash at the base. I need about four pesticide applications: herbicide early, then insecticide two or three times for aphids and armyworm.

My summer maize will be sown immediately after wheat harvest in early June. I use no-tillage direct seeding — there is no time to plough between wheat harvest and maize sowing, and Denghai 605 hybrid seed performs well with this method. Maize needs less fertilizer than wheat in my experience, about 24 kg nitrogen per mu, with some basal compound fertilizer. I irrigate twice, usually at the jointing stage and during grain filling. Three to four pesticide sprays are enough for maize — herbicide at sowing, then insecticide for corn borer.

For cotton, I keep 2.3 mu. Cotton is my cash crop, but it is very labor-intensive, and with my family working off-farm, I cannot manage more. I will rotary till the cotton plot in April, lay plastic mulch, and sow improved seed like 99-1 or Guoxinmian. Cotton needs more phosphorus and potassium than grain crops, and about 18 kg nitrogen per mu. I irrigate twice during the growing season. The biggest headache is pests — bollworm and aphids — so I need to spray pesticides many times, about 12 times this year. I used to spray 15 times, but now I try to combine sprays to save labor.

My land is divided: 5.5 mu for the wheat-maize rotation and 2.3 mu for cotton. This gives me enough grain for my household and some cotton income without overloading my limited labor.
